content: Go subprocess execution gotchas: 'go run' spawns the compiler then executes a temp binary as a child of the go tool - killing only the 'go run' process on timeout leaves the compiled binary or its own children as orphans; must set SysProcAttr{Setpgid:true} and kill the whole process group (syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)), not just cmd.Process.Kill(). GOCACHE must point to a writable directory per invocation/container or go build fails with 'permission denied' / 'failed to initialize build cache'; shared GOCACHE across concurrent generated-code compiles needs a writable dir with correct ownership (common Docker gotcha: golang image cache dir not writable by non-root user). Generated code with no go.mod fails module resolution - must generate/run 'go mod init' or use GOFLAGS=-mod=mod / GO111MODULE=off style workarounds, or pre-seed a template module. Compiled binaries and temp module dirs must be explicitly cleaned up (tempdir per task) or disk fills over time. Infinite loops/goroutine leaks in generated Go code hang past any timeout unless the process group is killed; cmd.Wait() can also block forever if a child inherited stdout/stderr pipes and keeps them open.
